sentences.text: OFFICE No. NOTE 02. 09.05.2025 Dr.VJP,J I.A.No.02 of 2025

The instant petition under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure / Section 430(1) of BNSS Act, 2023, has been filed by the Petitioner/Appellant/Accused, to enlarge the petitioner on bail by suspending the sentence and conviction of the Judgment dated 18.02.2025 in POCSO Sessions Case No. 49 of 2019 on the file of Special Judge for Speedy Trial of Offences under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
Nellore, pending disposal of the criminal appeal.

entities.text:

Nellore
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Heard Ms.Y.L.Siva Kalpana Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant.
Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor takes notice on behalf of the State.

Learned Counsel for the petitioner would submit that the victim in the present case as PW-2 deposed that at the instance of her maternal Aunt, she lodged a report against the accused in view of the money disputes between PW1, her husband Dr.VJPJ, with the accused.
Learned counsel would further submit that the accused used to work in the garage of sons of PW1.
In that regard, because of the money disputes, the case has been lodged against the accused.
Learned counsel would further submit that crucial witnesses in the present case are not examined by the prosecution.
There are serious discrepancies in the evidence of the prosecution witnesses and they have good grounds to succeed in the present appeal.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that the petitioner/Accused was found guilty and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 10 years and to pay fine of Rs.20,000/- for the offence under Section 376(2)(n)(i) of POCSO Act and in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for 6 months.

Accused is further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 5 years for the offence punishable under section 366 of IPC and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/- in default to under simple imprisonment for one month.

The accused is further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 3 years for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/-, in default, to undergo simple imprisonment for one month.
Learned counsel would further submit that Dr.VJPJ, this appeal may take considerable period of time for disposal.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that the petitioner is ready to furnish sureties to the satisfaction of the Court.
Learned counsel for the petitioner finally prays to allow the petition.
Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that against the petitioner one case which is alleged for the offence under Section 8(c) r/w 20(b)(i) of NDPS Act and it was ended in acquittal.
Another case for the offence under Section 324 and 509 of IPC was ended in compromise.
The suspect sheet is maintained against the petitioner.

sentences.text: Considering the submissions made and taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, in the light of the different versions depose by the victim before the Court, as rightly put by the learned counsel for the petitioner, this appeal may take considerable time for disposal.

In that view,
it is apposite to suspend the sentence of imprisonment passed against the petitioner on the following conditions:
i) Petitioner shall execute a personal bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty thousand only) with two sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the Special Court.
ii) Petitioner shall appear before the Special Court Dr.VJPJ, once in a month i.e., on the First Monday of every month till the disposal of the present appeal.
iii) Learned Trial Judge shall maintain a record of the presence of the petitioner before the Court and inform to this Court in case of any absence of the petitioner.
Admit.
List the matter in usual course.
Dr.VJP, J Note: CC today, B/o.
